operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are simple mixed-case (Railway_ID, From, Name, Level) with no spaces; double-quote them and compare case-insensitively.
Tiny DB (10/9/7/4 rows); no huge-table sampling needed, but read_schema must still handle max_rows_per_table path.
Declared types are only INT and TEXT; no date/time/bool/bit/year types, so no Date/Time/Bool fuzzers dispatch here.
Text-stored dates/years: railway.Built ('1901','1902'), manager.Working_year_starts ('2003'), railway_manage.From_Year ('2010') are TEXT -> String fuzzer, not Date.
Text-stored times: train.Arrival ('08:54','23:44') is TEXT -> String fuzzer, not Time.
railway.Built has a dirty long value '1902 Midland Railway 1000 was rebuilt in' mixed with plain years; String length range will be wide.
railway.Wheels values like '4-4-0','0-6-0T' are TEXT; String fuzzer will treat as generic strings.
train.Railway_ID FK -> railway.Railway_ID, parent exists and is unique PK; railway_manage has two FKs to railway and manager, both valid.
railway_manage has composite PK (Railway_ID, Manager_ID); both members are also FK columns -> composite-PK member max_l0=30 path.
No NOT NULL constraints (notnull=0 everywhere); no CHECK/UNIQUE beyond PKs; no self-references; no dangling FKs.
All columns null_rate 0.0 in original; storage classes match declared types (integer/text) with no contradictions.
railway_manage.Railway_ID distinct=4 but railway has 10 rows; FK child draws from parent's final values with replacement, so ties/duplicates expected.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INT columns (Railway_ID, Train_ID, Manager_ID, Age, Level, FK ints) with scale=0, precision=0, is_int=True; range [-1,1] then +-1/+-2 perturbation -> tiny ints, likely colliding with PKs.
String fuzzer on all TEXT columns with default length [0,20]; fresh strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() plus 0.5 contaminate -> implausible names, builders, locations.
String fuzzer on Built/Working_year_starts/From_Year/Arrival will NOT produce date/time-shaped values (no Date/Time dispatch), so date predicates in gold SQL likely get no matching rows -> FN risk.
String fuzzer on Wheels/ObjectNumber/Train_Num will not preserve '4-4-0' or '1975-7006' patterns; FORMAT-style predicates miss -> FN.
Number fuzzer on Age/Level draws from [-1,1] +-1/+-2, ignoring original 45-55 / 5-12 ranges -> RANGE predicates (age>50, level>10) mostly false -> FN.
Number fuzzer on FK ints draws from parent's final values with replacement, so FK joins work but produce many-to-one ties; DISTINCT/COUNT queries may still be plausible.
Composite PK (Railway_ID, Manager_ID) gets max_l0=30 fresh draws then reuse -> duplicate pairs dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys, shrinking railway_manage.
Small table sizes (choose_table_sizes: level0 1+30u, x4 per level, cap 2500) -> instances of tens to hundreds of rows, far larger than originals (4-10 rows).
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python; rows violating PK/unique dropped, others inserted -> some columns may end up with NULLs only if parent empty (unlikely here).
String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like strings (Train_Num '51195', ObjectNumber '1975-7006' not int-like) -> limited numeric-string preservation.
Date/Time fuzzers never invoked; any gold SQL comparing Arrival to a time literal or Built to a year literal will see String-fuzzer values -> FP/FN from type mismatch.
Literal pool from train SQL will seed e.g. '08:54', '1901', 'SECR' into String columns; p=0.2 element reuse gives some plausible values but mostly fresh strings.
